title: Alibaba to ban employees from using Anthropic's coding tool, source says

reading.body:
This is a case of a vendor embedding a covert detection mechanism inside a shipped developer tool, not a case of a model producing wrong output. The markers were placed in the system prompt the tool sends to the model, so the manipulation sat in the request-construction layer rather than in the model itself. The mechanism activated only under a specific configuration, a custom API base URL, which means it was invisible to the default user path and visible only to the population it was aimed at.

Catching this required reading the client binary or intercepting its outbound requests, which is what the inspecting developer did. The obfuscation, base64 strings decoded with an XOR key, was designed to survive casual inspection rather than determined analysis. The reported bypasses, changing the hostname or timezone or patching the binary, indicate the mechanism was not robust, which is a separate matter from whether it was disclosed.

What is not established is Anthropic's intent beyond its own public description of the feature as an experiment, and the reporting does not show that any user data was transmitted or that the markers caused harm. Alibaba's reported ban rests on an allegation of backdoor risk attributed to an unnamed source, and an allegation is not a finding.

reports.title: Claude Code Is Steganographically Marking Requests
Anthropic is removing its covert code for catching Chinese competitors
Claude Code’s hidden tracker was an “experiment,” says Anthropic
Alibaba to ban employees from using Anthropic's coding tool, source says

summary:
A developer inspecting Claude Code version 2.1.196 found hidden markers embedded in the system prompt sent to the model. The tool silently alters the date string, swapping the apostrophe in "Today's" and changing date separators from hyphens to slashes, based on the API base URL and system timezone. The trigger is the ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL setting. Domain and keyword lists are stored as base64 strings and decoded with an XOR key. The keyword list includes names like deepseek, moonshot, and zhipu, while the domain list covers Chinese tech companies and proxy or reseller gateways.

For most users the feature stays inactive, since it only activates when a custom base URL is set. The author suggests Anthropic likely wants to detect resellers, unauthorized gateways, and distillation pipelines, but criticizes the hidden approach. The article notes the bypass is trivial, through changing the hostname, timezone, or patching the binary. No next steps are stated.
